a proxied request keeps its framing: a GET reaches the backend without `Transfer-Encoding`, and a POST with a 13-byte JSON body reaches it with `Content-Length: 13`, as it does when sent to the backend directly.
an upstream redirect becomes 502 `Upstream redirect is not allowed` with no `Location`, and an upstream `Set-Cookie` never reaches the client.
a proxied response carries a single `Date` and a single `Server` header.
`.`/`..` segments and backslashes, percent-encoded at any depth, answer 400 `Invalid backend path` before any credential check, on HTTP and WebSocket.

a WebSocket with the cookie and the ingress `Origin` is bridged to the backend, which echoes frames and receives no cookie, `Origin`, session key or `session_api_key` parameter; a path the backend does not upgrade (the root route) is accepted and then closed with 1011.
a WebSocket without the ingress `Origin`, without a valid cookie for this app, or with only the session key is refused at the handshake with 403.
a WebSocket subprotocol requested by the client reaches the backend and is negotiated through the bridge.

`DELETE /app-backends/{name}/session` answers 204 with a `Max-Age=0` cookie, closes that session's bridged WebSocket and makes its cookie 401, while other sessions of the app keep working; it needs the key and a control origin but no cookie.

stopping or disabling the backend closes bridged WebSockets and makes the bridge answer 503; after the backend starts again on a new port, old cookies get 401 and a new session works. A backend that dies while ready is reported `unhealthy` (exited) by a status poll, after which the bridge answers 503, and once it starts again a session minted before the crash gets 401 because sessions are bound to the backend's port.
once a ready backend's process has exited, the bridge answers 503 `Canvas App backend is not ready` without waiting for anyone to poll the backend's status.

with `trust_forwarded_headers` on, `X-Forwarded-Host` naming the ingress is accepted from a request whose `Host` is not, and a forwarded `https` that does not match the ingress answers 421; turned off again, the same header is ignored.
after a server restart the backend is stopped (the bridge answers 503), its prepared revision survives so it starts without a new prepare, and cookies minted before the restart get 401.
an idle bridged WebSocket is closed when its session expires 300 s after the bootstrap, and its cookie then gets 401.
uninstalling the app closes its bridged WebSockets, stops its backend and makes the bridge answer 503 to old cookies and new bootstraps.

`GET /v1/models` lists one `{"id": "openhands_<profile>", "object": "model", "created": 0, "owned_by": "openhands"}` per saved LLM profile, sorted by id, and follows renames and deletes of profiles at once.

with session keys configured, all three routes accept the key as `Authorization: Bearer` or as `X-Session-API-Key`, and answer 401 `Unauthorized` to a missing or wrong key before the body is validated, while `/api/*` still refuses Bearer.
a server with no session keys serves `/v1` without any credential and with any Bearer value.

`POST /v1/chat/completions` on a real model returns a `chat.completion` whose single choice carries the agent's final answer with `finish_reason` `stop`, echoes the model, reports usage, and names a new finished conversation in `X-OpenHands-ServerConversation-ID`.
`system` and `developer` messages become the new conversation's `agent_context.system_message_suffix` (in the system prompt) and never appear as user messages.
a new conversation receives only the last user message of `messages[]`; earlier user and assistant turns are dropped and stored nowhere.

`stream: true` answers `text/event-stream` with the conversation header and the frames role, whole content, `finish_reason` `stop`, usage (only with `stream_options.include_usage`) and `[DONE]`; a failing streaming request is a plain JSON error, not an SSE frame.
sending `X-OpenHands-ServerConversation-ID` back appends the new user message to that conversation, reruns it (live on its events socket) and returns the same id.
after a server restart the header still continues the persisted conversation.
a well-formed but unknown id in the header creates the conversation with exactly that id; a malformed id is 422 and creates nothing.

on a continued conversation the requested model must still exist (404 otherwise) but is not applied: the conversation keeps its own LLM and system suffix, and the other profile's provider is never called.
`usage` on a continued conversation reports that request's tokens, not the conversation's running total (reproduces a real bug).
two overlapping requests on one conversation each get the answer to their own turn (reproduces a real bug: the first request returns the second request's answer).
the agent runs its own tools in the server workspace (a file appears there), the answer carries no `tool_calls`, and the client's `tools`/`tool_choice` are ignored.

bad chat input fails before any conversation exists: 400 without a user message or with a bad content part, 404 for a model without the `openhands_` prefix or an unknown profile, 400 for an invalid profile name, 422 for schema errors.
`X-OpenHands-Observability-*` headers are stored on the new conversation (chat and responses); invalid values are 422 before anything runs.
a run that ends in `error` answers 500 with the rewritten body (`exception` `500: Agent run ended with status: error`), without the conversation header, and leaves the conversation in `error`.
with confirmation mode saved in the settings, a new conversation that stops `waiting_for_confirmation` answers 409 at once.
a continued conversation that stops `waiting_for_confirmation` must also answer 409 promptly (reproduces a real bug: it waits out 120 s and answers 504).
when `max_concurrent_runs` is full a new gateway conversation is refused with 429 and nothing is created; the same request succeeds once a slot is free.
on a continued conversation a 429 must also leave nothing behind, so a client retry is safe (reproduces a real bug: each refused try appends the user message again).
a run longer than the fixed 120 s answers 504 `Agent run timed out`, and the run keeps going server-side.

`POST /v1/responses` on a real model returns a completed `response` with one `output_text` message equal to the agent's final answer, echoes `instructions` and `metadata`, and puts the instructions in the system suffix.

every responses call is a new conversation (the conversation header is ignored); replayed items become one user message wrapped in `<message role="...">` markers, and developer items go to the system suffix.
`stream`, `store: true` and `previous_response_id` are 400 before anything else is checked, bad input is 400 or 422, an unknown model 404, and nothing is created.
the official OpenAI Python SDK lists models, reads the conversation header through `with_raw_response`, continues the conversation with `extra_headers`, parses a stream and creates a response.
loading a conversation writes `owner_lease.json` in its directory with generation 1, the server's pid and host, and an expiry about 45 s ahead.
while the server lives, the lease's `expires_at` moves forward within 15 s, with the same owner and generation.
a graceful restart deletes the lease of every loaded conversation, catalog reads do not claim it again, and the next load claims generation 1 under the new pid.
after a SIGKILL the lease still names the dead pid; the restarted server takes it over on first load with generation 2 and logs the takeover.

a conversation SIGKILLed during a tool call is loaded again at startup, comes back `error` with one `AgentErrorEvent` answering the interrupted call and no observation, and the resumed run hands that error to the model.
a conversation's title, tags and events, the settings, a stored secret and the LLM profiles read back unchanged after a graceful restart and after a SIGKILL.

after a real model run, the provider key, a stored secret and a conversation secret appear nowhere in the run's persisted files or the server log, while the server still hands out the provider key and the stored secret and keeps the conversation secret encrypted in its registry.
a second server sharing the conversations directory lists, counts and reads conversations that existed when it started, without claiming their leases.

while the owner lives, the second server cannot load the conversation: event reads, sending a message, `/run` and `agent_final_response` are 404, PATCH is `success: false`, pause, interrupt and DELETE are 400, its events socket closes 4004, and nothing changes.
once the owner is SIGKILLed, the second server takes the conversation over at once (generation 2, its pid) with the same events, and the restarted owner is now the one refused.
a title the owner stored after the second server started survives the second server's takeover, in its GET and in `meta.json`.
an owner that stops renewing (frozen, pid alive) loses the lease once it expires, and after it resumes its writes are refused and never reach disk.
a write refused for lost ownership answers a 4xx and leaves no trace: the stale owner's own GET does not report the refused title.
with `lease_ttl_seconds` 0 no lease file is written and a second server loads and writes the same conversation concurrently.

an idle conversation is unloaded at the first eviction pass after its TTL (lease deleted, `Evicted idle` logged), stays listed with its title and status, and loads again with the same events on the next access.
the same pass keeps a conversation with an open events socket and a running one loaded; once the socket closes and the run is interrupted, the next pass unloads both.
with every run slot taken, `POST <redacted:session-cookie>` answers 429 and creates nothing, on disk or in the catalog; the same request succeeds once the slot is free.
the configuration file is applied and an `OH_*` variable overrides the same field (seen through the lease TTL).
`OH_<FIELD>_IS_NONE=1` clears a value the configuration file sets, as a non-null `OH_*` value replaces it (seen through `app_backend_public_url` in `/server_info`).
a non-numeric `OH_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS` or an out-of-range limit in the configuration file stops the server during startup instead of serving with a default.

an `OH_*` boolean other than `1`/`true` is read as false (it overrides a `true` in the configuration file) and a `Literal` variable outside its choices falls back to the default; the server starts either way, while the same invalid choice in the file stops startup.
a server that defaulted its own per-process `TMUX_TMPDIR` removes that directory when it stops.

with the Docker runtime, `conversation_storage_retention_days` archives a stopped conversation inactive past the limit (events readable, resume and proxied routes 410, runtime directory gone), and `conversation_storage_disk_budget` sheds a stopped workspace's gitignored directories while keeping its files (blocked here: no Docker daemon).
a run's events reach `POST {base_url}/events/<conversation id hex, no dashes>` as JSON arrays, through the agent's reply and the `finished` status update.
every webhook request carries `Content-Type: application/json` and the server's first session key as `X-Session-API-Key`.
each attach of a conversation (its creation, and its first use after a restart) posts a transient `ConversationStateUpdateEvent` with key `full_state`.
a streaming run's `StreamingDeltaEvent`s reach the events WebSocket but never a webhook.
creating a conversation POSTs its `ConversationInfo` to `{base_url}/conversations`.
pausing, interrupting, updating and deleting a conversation each POST its info again (`paused`, `paused`, the new title, `deleting`).
a webhook's `headers` and a `base_url` path prefix apply to both event and conversation posts.
once `event_buffer_size` events are queued they are posted at once, without waiting for `flush_delay`.
events that arrive while a batch is in flight are posted as soon as the buffer is full again, not held until `flush_delay` (reproduces a real delay; see Gotchas).
a partial buffer is posted `flush_delay` seconds after its first event; later events do not restart the timer.

the `WebhookSpec` field descriptions published in the OpenAPI schema (the item type of `POST /api/init`'s `webhooks`) state the real event path and flush timer (reproduces a documentation bug; see Gotchas).
deleting a conversation posts its queued events before the `DELETE` returns, and a graceful server stop posts every conversation's queue.
`max_batch_bytes` caps each request (an event larger than it is posted alone), and `max_queue_size` and `max_queue_bytes` drop the oldest queued events with a warning.
a receiver that answers 500 gets `num_retries + 1` attempts per event batch and per conversation post.
a batch that exhausted its retries is requeued and sent again on the next flush, not dropped.
a slow webhook receiver must not keep a conversation that reports `finished` from accepting a new run (reproduces a real 409; see Gotchas).
`OH_WEBHOOKS_0_*` environment variables configure a webhook and override the config file's first webhook field by field.
no exporter, or the `http` exporter without consent, delivers nothing.
with the `http` exporter and consent, `server_started` arrives at boot and `server_stopped` at a graceful stop, as `{"schema_version": 1, "events": [...]}` with the configured Bearer token.
a run emits `conversation_created` and `conversation_finished` under the request's `user_id`, with a pseudonymous `conversation_ref` and without the prompt or the conversation id.

an unhandled 500 emits `request_failed` with the route template (never the concrete path), the exception class and the response's `error_id`, attributed to `X-OpenHands-Telemetry-Distinct-Id`, without the exception message.
a run that ends in `error` emits `conversation_failed` (`terminal_status` `error`) and `conversation_error` with the error code as `error_class`, without the error's detail text.
`conversation_finished` reports token and cost buckets from the run's real usage (reproduces a real gap; see Gotchas).
granting or denying consent with `PATCH /api/settings` `misc_settings_diff` starts or stops delivery immediately, and persisted consent enables telemetry after a restart.
`OH_TELEMETRY_CONSENT=denied` with `OH_TELEMETRY_CONSENT_MODE=override` beats a granted setting.
`DO_NOT_TRACK=1` beats every consent source.

without a salt `conversation_ref` is keyed by `OH_SECRET_KEY` (the same ref across restarts); `OH_TELEMETRY_SALT` re-keys it (again the same across restarts), and `OH_TELEMETRY_DEPLOYMENT_KIND` tags every event.
the `TelemetrySpec.salt` description published in the OpenAPI schema states the real fallback key (reproduces a documentation bug; see Gotchas).
a dormant pod sends nothing until `POST /api/init` delivers `telemetry` and `webhooks`; then `server_started`, conversation telemetry and webhooks flow.
events from an initialized deferred pod report `deferred_init: true` (reproduces a real mislabel; see Gotchas).

`Workspace(host=...)` returns a `RemoteWorkspace` whose `execute_command` returns the command's exit code, stdout and stderr, runs in the given `cwd`, gives up after `timeout` with exit `-1` and `timeout_occurred`; `alive` and `get_server_info()` match the server.

with a wrong `api_key`, `execute_command` and `file_upload` report a 401 failure instead of raising, creating a conversation raises a 401 `HTTPStatusError`, and the server records no command, file or conversation.
`start_command` returns a command id at once, `get_command_output` shows no exit code while it runs, `stop_command` ends it (no later output), and stopping an unknown id is a no-op.

`file_upload` (from a path or from bytes) and `file_download` round-trip a binary file byte for byte; a missing remote file or a relative destination reports `success: false` with the server's 404 or 400 and leaves no local file.
`git_changes` (a path relative to `working_dir`) and `git_diff` return what the server's git routes return for a repository with a modified and an untracked file.

`get_llm()` resolves the server's active LLM profile with a usable key, `get_llm(profile_name=...)` a named one (unknown names raise `FileNotFoundError`), `get_secrets()` returns `LookupSecret` references without values, and `get_mcp_config()` is empty on a fresh server.

`AsyncRemoteWorkspace` runs a command, starts, reads and stops a background command, uploads and downloads a file, reads git changes, a git diff and server info, and closes its client on context exit.

a `RemoteWorkspace(runtime_conversation_id=...)` routes through `<redacted:session-cookie>/{id}/...`: commands default to the conversation's workspace and land in its own bash history, paths outside that workspace are refused with 422, and an unknown conversation gives 404.
`get_runtime_session_key()` and `release_runtime()` hand out a scoped worker key and stop a conversation's runtime on a server with a Docker conversation runtime.

`Conversation(agent, workspace=RemoteWorkspace)` returns a `RemoteConversation` that creates the server conversation with the agent, working directory, tags and `max_iteration_per_run`; `send_message` stores the message without running and the agent's key is not echoed back.

`RemoteConversation.create(workspace, StartConversationRequest(...))` creates the conversation with the requested id from server-built `agent_settings`, tags and iteration limit, and runs its `initial_message`; repeating the same request returns the same conversation and adds no conversation or message.

`RemoteConversation.create(workspace, StartConversationRequest(agent_profile_id=...))` builds the agent from a saved agent profile (its LLM profile, tool selection and system message suffix), records the launched profile and runs the `initial_message` to `finished`; `get_secrets(agent_profile_id=...)` returns only the profile's `secret_refs`.
`send_message` plus a blocking `run()` returns once the agent finished; the server reports `finished` and the file the agent wrote exists.
callbacks receive the run's events live over the events WebSocket, and after `run()` the callback counts and `state.events` match the server's persisted events kind by kind.
`conversation_stats` and `state.execution_status` read back the server's numbers (accumulated cost and prompt tokens of the agent's LLM).

with a `Stop` hook that refuses the first stop (exit 2), a blocking `run()` returns only after the extra agent turn the hook forced: the server is `finished` when `run()` returns, and `state.events` already holds both stop `HookExecutionEvent`s (blocked, then allowed) and the hook's feedback, matching the server kind by kind.

`Conversation(client_tools=[ClientToolSpec(...)])` delivers the model's call to the callbacks as a typed `ClientAction_<name>` `ActionEvent`, the server acknowledges it with a `ClientToolObservation` and finishes, and a second program that attaches without `client_tools` replays those events.
with a `stream=True` agent LLM, callbacks receive the run's `StreamingDeltaEvent` frames live and the server stores none of them.
`Conversation(token_callbacks=[...])` on a remote workspace calls the token callbacks with the run's streamed deltas.
streamed deltas stay out of `state.events`, which keeps matching the server's stored events.

an agent LLM with `log_completions=True` gets one log file per model call in its `log_completions_folder`, written by the client from the `LLMCompletionLogEvent`s the server streams and stores (the server writes no file).

a second program reattaches by id with `RemoteConversation.attach()` or `Conversation(conversation_id=...)` and replays the same history without creating anything; `attach()` on an unknown id raises 404 while `Conversation(conversation_id=<new id>)` creates that id.

attaching to a conversation with more than 100 stored events pages through the whole history: `state.events` holds the server's events in the server's order (plus the one unpersisted socket snapshot), and the first reads of `state.confirmation_policy`, `state.security_analyzer`, `state.hook_config` and `state.agent` equal the server's.
reading `state.confirmation_policy`, `state.security_analyzer`, `state.agent` and `is_confirmation_mode_active` a second time gives the same answer as the first.
`ask_agent()` answers without adding events, `generate_title()` returns a title within `max_length` without adding events, and `set_title()` changes the server's title.
`fork(title=..., tags=...)` returns a `RemoteConversation` for a new server conversation with the same history, the title and the tags; `fork(agent=...)` is refused client-side.

`fork(from_event_id=..., reset_metrics=False)` returns a fork whose history ends at that event (its HEAD) with the source's stats, and `navigate_to(None)` and `navigate_to(event_id)` move the fork's HEAD without changing its events.
`Conversation(plugins=[PluginSource(...)])` with inline URL credentials stores the `plugins` tag with the credentials masked, and the token reaches no server state.

`set_confirmation_policy(AlwaysConfirm())` makes `run()` return at `waiting_for_confirmation`; `reject_pending_actions()` records a `UserRejectObservation`, never runs the action and leaves the conversation `idle`.
`pause()` from another thread during a blocking `run()` lets the tool step in flight finish, makes `run()` return with `paused` and a `PauseEvent`, and a later `run()` resumes to `finished`.

`interrupt()` from another thread while a blocking `run()` waits on a model call makes `run()` return at once without raising, at `paused` with one `InterruptEvent` and no `PauseEvent`, and a later `run()` reaches `finished`.

`run(timeout=...)` raises `ConversationRunError` wrapping a `TimeoutError` on time while the server keeps running, and a second `run()` joins the run in flight (the server's 409 is not an error) and returns at `finished`.
a second `run()` also joins a run whose current tool call lasts longer than 30 s, instead of raising.
when the server's stuck detector stops a looping agent, `run()` raises `ConversationRunError` ("got stuck") at once and the server reports `stuck`.
`update_secrets()` with a plain value and with a `LookupSecret` from `get_secrets()` makes both available to the agent's commands, masked in observations and not stored in plaintext.
when the model provider rejects the key, `run()` raises `ConversationRunError` carrying the server's `ConversationErrorEvent` code, and the server reports `error`.

a live `RemoteConversation` survives a server restart: its events socket reconnects, a new message runs to `finished`, and `state.events` again matches the server.
an event the server records while a live `RemoteConversation`'s events socket is down reaches its callbacks once the socket is back, not only `state.events`.
after a restart a new program reattaches to a finished conversation, sees the same history, and continues it to `finished`.

a tool registered in the client process is sent as `tool_module_qualnames`, imported by a server started with `OH_EXTRA_PYTHON_PATH`, and runs on the server when the agent calls it; a client-registered module the server cannot import is only a logged warning; reattaching from a process without the module raises `ImportError` naming the tool.
a conversation whose agent names a tool from a module the server cannot import fails with a client error (a 4xx, or a recorded conversation error), never with a 500.
`close()` keeps the server conversation when `delete_on_close=False` and deletes it when the `Conversation(...)` factory's default `delete_on_close=True` applies.

`ServerClient` (through `ConversationManager.server` and `AgentServerClient.server`) reads `/alive`, `/health`, `/ready`, `/server_info` and `/` with the server's own values, the probes without a key; the version-gated clients (`HooksClient`, `WorkspacesClient`, `MCPClient`) read `/server_info` once per transport, accept this server and return its data.

a missing or wrong key rejects with an `HttpError` (`status` 401, `detail` `Unauthorized`, recognized by `isHttpError`), a 404 and a 422 carry the server's `detail` and `validationErrors`, while an unreachable host and a client timeout reject with plain errors.
`RemoteWorkspace.executeCommand` returns stdout, stderr and the exit code of a command run in the given `cwd`, and exit `-1` once the command's own timeout kills it.

`RemoteWorkspace.uploadText`/`fileUpload` and `downloadAsText`, and `FileClient.downloadFile`/`uploadTextFile`, round-trip files (bytes exact through `FileClient`); a missing file, a relative path and a directory reject with the server's 404 and 400.
`RemoteWorkspace.downloadAsBlob` returns a binary file byte for byte.

a `RemoteWorkspace` with `conversationId` routes through `<redacted:session-cookie>/{id}/bash|file/...`: commands default to the conversation's workspace and land in its own bash history, paths and `cwd` outside it get 422, an unknown conversation 404.

`RemoteWorkspace.gitChanges` and `gitDiff` return the server's changes and diff for a repository, globally and through `<redacted:session-cookie>/{id}/git/...` for a scoped workspace, and wrap a 422 (path outside the conversation workspace) or 401 in an `Error` whose `cause` is the `HttpError`.
the statuses `gitChanges` returns type-check as the exported `GitChange['status']`, as they do against the client's generated contract.

`RemoteWorkspace.bash` starts a background command, finds its output with `searchEvents`, reads events one at a time and in batches (unknown ids are `null`), stops a running command, treats an unknown id as already stopped, and `clearEvents` empties the history.
`BashWebSocketClient` in Node delivers the bash events of a command (replayed with `resendMode: 'all'`) to its callback without errors.

`startWorkspaceSession(id)` answers with the workspace base URL that serves the conversation's files, `deleteWorkspaceSession()` succeeds, a mismatched scoped id is refused before any request, and no key is 401.
`RemoteConversation.start()` creates the server conversation with the client's agent (LLM, tools), working directory and `max_iterations`, and rebinds its workspace to the new conversation.

a reattached `RemoteConversation` stores a `sendMessage` without running, `run()` drives a real model to `finished`, the `hookConfig` given at creation runs before the tool call and is reported by `getHookConfig()`, the client reads the agent's file, stats, final response and trajectory ZIP, and `RemoteState` reports the server's status, agent, workspace, policy and persistence directory.
`RemoteEventsList` counts, searches (source, fully-qualified kind, body, pages), fetches events by id and iterates the same events the server stores.

`RemoteEventsList.search({kind: 'MessageEvent'})` and `count({kind: 'MessageEvent'})`, the short kind its own docs show (`ActionEvent, MessageEvent`), find the same events as the fully-qualified kind.

`ConversationEventStream` on Node's global `WebSocket` authenticates with the first frame, replays the stored events with `resend_mode: 'all'`, sends a user message that runs the agent to `finished` on the same socket, and reports a wrong key as a 4001 close.
`RemoteConversation.startWebSocketClient()` in Node delivers the conversation's events to the conversation callback without errors.
`setTitle` and `setConfirmationPolicy` change the server's title and policy.

under `AlwaysConfirm`, `sendConfirmationResponse(false, reason)` records one `UserRejectObservation` with that reason and leaves the command unrun, `sendConfirmationResponse(true)` runs the pending command, and `updateSecrets` (a string and a function value) puts both values into that command's shell without any event containing them.

confirmed_bugs.title: Skills sync reports success after its git fetch fails
confirmed_bugs.expected: Report an unsuccessful forced refresh when its origin cannot be fetched.
confirmed_bugs.actual: A direct git fetch proves the configured origin is unreachable, but POST /api/skills/sync returns status=success and Skills repository synced successfully.
confirmed_bugs.notes: Response metadata defect; retaining the cached clone is permissible, but the forced sync result is inaccurate.

confirmed_bugs.title: Skills sync does not refresh the marketplace catalog cache
confirmed_bugs.expected: After sync brings a newly listed skill into the clone, marketplace catalog lists that entry.
confirmed_bugs.actual: Sync succeeds and the cloned skill and manifest entry exist, but the catalog still omits qa-f25-pub-extra; one warmed catalog retains its prior entry, and the second retains a cached empty result.
confirmed_bugs.notes: Independent from the public manifest-path issue: the local stand-in has a valid marketplaces/default.json. Sync invalidates only public-skills cache, leaving the catalog TTL cache.

confirmed_bugs.title: Manifestless repository plugins inherit the cache hash in their name
confirmed_bugs.expected: A manifestless repository installs under its repository directory name.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The source qa-f26-src installs as qa-f26-src-<16 hex>, derived from its URL-hashed cache directory.
confirmed_bugs.notes: Metadata/naming defect; fixture is removed before the assertion.

confirmed_bugs.title: A resumed conversation still activates a disabled plugin skill
confirmed_bugs.expected: A resumed turn follows the plugin enabled state on disk.
confirmed_bugs.actual: After disabling the plugin and restarting, its hook no longer runs, but its first slash command still has activated_skills=[qa-f26-inst:qa-hello] on the user message.
confirmed_bugs.notes: Two real DeepSeek turns per proof. The later include_skills GET assertion is not reached; the live socket activation itself is proven twice.

confirmed_bugs.title: A sub-agent with an absent configured skill causes message POST 500
confirmed_bugs.expected: Reject invalid agent configuration or return a client error when it is used.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The conversation is created, but appending a user message returns 500 Skill ... not found but was given to agent ...
confirmed_bugs.notes: Bad configuration/error-mapping defect, not a model failure.

confirmed_bugs.title: Resuming without the registered custom tool module returns an unhandled 500
confirmed_bugs.expected: Report a missing custom-module prerequisite with a controlled client error.
confirmed_bugs.actual: After the real custom-tool turn persists its observation, restart without its module makes message POST return 500 because the observation discriminator is not registered.
confirmed_bugs.notes: The initial custom tool executes successfully on real DeepSeek in both proofs; missing-module errors are not claimed as successful restores.

confirmed_bugs.title: Server info advertises the browser despite enable_browser=false
confirmed_bugs.expected: The server-info usable_tools agrees with the config-aware catalog.
confirmed_bugs.actual: Catalog browser usability is false on the disabled server, but server_info still includes browser_tool_set.
confirmed_bugs.notes: Metadata inconsistency. The fresh supplement retains the real host Chromium rather than requiring an unnecessary cache symlink.

confirmed_bugs.title: Disabled-browser servers still list the browser-only built-in agent
confirmed_bugs.expected: Exclude the browser-only web-researcher when enable_browser=false.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The catalog marks browser_tool_set unusable, but built-in discovery still returns web-researcher.
confirmed_bugs.notes: Only discovery was driven; no browser delegation or configuration bypass is claimed.

confirmed_bugs.title: The browser availability probe ignores PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH
confirmed_bugs.expected: Find the real Chromium binary installed solely under PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH.
confirmed_bugs.actual: Two fresh Chromium-free layout-image containers report the browser unusable with the configured Playwright path. Linking the same binary into HOME/.cache/ms-playwright makes the catalog usable; removing that link reproduces the failure.
confirmed_bugs.notes: The real host Chromium binary is mounted read-only; only probe/catalog usability is asserted, not a navigation test. Each container is removed after its attached-run proof.

confirmed_bugs.title: Canvas bridge trusts a forwarded scheme despite its setting
confirmed_bugs.expected: With trust_forwarded_headers disabled, X-Forwarded-Proto should not alter an otherwise valid request.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The same session bootstrap succeeds without the header and returns 421 when X-Forwarded-Proto: https is supplied.

confirmed_bugs.title: Canvas bare-root query parameter changes the proxied path
confirmed_bugs.expected: ?path=echo on the bare app root should reach the root with the query unchanged.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The proxy sends the request to /echo, whereas the trailing-slash root preserves /.

confirmed_bugs.title: Canvas proxy sends duplicate Date and Server headers
confirmed_bugs.expected: A proxied response should contain one Date and one Server header.
confirmed_bugs.actual: Uvicorn adds its headers alongside copied backend headers, producing comma-joined duplicate values.

confirmed_bugs.title: Canvas WebSocket bridge loses requested subprotocol
confirmed_bugs.expected: The bridge should negotiate qa.v1 exactly as the directly contacted backend does.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The direct socket selects qa.v1; the proxied socket selects no protocol and reports protocol none, breaking browser clients that require a subprotocol.

confirmed_bugs.title: Canvas bridge keeps crashed backend ready until status polling
confirmed_bugs.expected: After the backend process exits, requests should return 503 backend not ready.
confirmed_bugs.actual: Without a status poll, requests return 502 Conversation container unreachable for the entire 15-second observation.

confirmed_bugs.title: OpenAI continuation usage includes previous turns
confirmed_bugs.expected: The second request should report its own 3 prompt, 2 completion and 5 total tokens.
confirmed_bugs.actual: It reports accumulated 13 prompt, 7 completion and 20 total tokens although per-call usage is available.

confirmed_bugs.title: Overlapping OpenAI requests receive the later turn's answer
confirmed_bugs.expected: Request X should receive its stored QA_F30_RACE_B answer; request Y should receive QA_F30_RACE_C.
confirmed_bugs.actual: Both requests receive QA_F30_RACE_C although the server stores the correct separate B and C agent messages.

confirmed_bugs.title: OpenAI continuation waits 120 seconds at confirmation
confirmed_bugs.expected: A continued conversation awaiting confirmation should return 409 promptly, like a new one.
confirmed_bugs.actual: It remains waiting_for_confirmation with the proposed command unrun, then returns 504 after the fixed 120-second gateway timeout.

confirmed_bugs.title: Rejected OpenAI continuations persist duplicate user turns
confirmed_bugs.expected: A 429 should leave the conversation unchanged so an OpenAI retry is safe.
confirmed_bugs.actual: Each refused request appends the user message; two 429 responses leave two copies.

confirmed_bugs.title: Second-server takeover overwrites newer conversation metadata
confirmed_bugs.expected: The title last persisted by the first owner should survive takeover.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The second server rewrites meta.json with its startup catalog's older title, losing the owner's later rename.
notes: Isolated copied recipe adjusts only exited-zombie setup observation; frozen product source and bug assertion unchanged. See F31-zombie-adaptation.md.

confirmed_bugs.title: Rejected stale-owner write changes its GET state and returns 500
confirmed_bugs.expected: A lost-ownership PATCH should give a client error and leave visible state unchanged.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The guarded save refuses the write and disk remains correct, but the stale owner's GET reports the refused title; PATCH returns 500.

confirmed_bugs.title: Explicit environment null cannot clear a configured value
confirmed_bugs.expected: OH_APP_BACKEND_PUBLIC_URL_IS_NONE=1 should clear the URL and capability even when the config file sets it.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The file's URL remains advertised because merge keeps an earlier value when the environment supplies None. The same behavior prevents environment-based disabling of a configured idle TTL.

confirmed_bugs.title: Server-selected per-process tmux directory survives shutdown
confirmed_bugs.expected: The per-process TMUX_TMPDIR selected by the server should disappear after graceful stop.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The directory remains; the recipe's cleanup trap removes it after recording the failed assertion.
notes: Isolated copied recipe adjusts only exited-zombie setup observation; frozen product source and bug assertion unchanged. See F31-zombie-adaptation.md.

confirmed_bugs.title: Full webhook buffer waits behind an in-flight batch
confirmed_bugs.expected: The queued user message should reach the sink within ten seconds once the buffer fills.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The first batch is posted, while a second full buffer waits for the long flush timer or a later close.

confirmed_bugs.title: Webhook schema documents the wrong event path and timer
confirmed_bugs.expected: OpenAPI should describe the per-conversation event path and a timer started by the first event.
confirmed_bugs.actual: It says events go to /events and the timer resets with every new event; live behavior differs.

confirmed_bugs.title: Slow webhook causes 409 after the conversation reports finished
confirmed_bugs.expected: A finished conversation should accept a new run regardless of receiver latency.
confirmed_bugs.actual: A fast receiver permits POST /run; a 15-second receiver makes it return 409 Conversation already running while GET says finished.

confirmed_bugs.title: Conversation outcome telemetry misses real token and cost usage
confirmed_bugs.expected: A real model run's outcome should contain measured usage buckets.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The conversation has positive token usage but outcome total_tokens_bucket and cost_bucket are unknown.

confirmed_bugs.title: Telemetry schema promises a random fallback instead of secret key
confirmed_bugs.expected: The salt description should state that the configured secret key is the first fallback.
confirmed_bugs.actual: It promises per-process random salt and unlinkability across runs although the secret-key-derived reference remains stable across restarts.

confirmed_bugs.title: Python remote conversations ignore token callbacks
confirmed_bugs.expected: Token callbacks should receive streamed deltas supplied to the remote conversation.
confirmed_bugs.actual: Event callbacks see deltas, but the token callback is never called.

confirmed_bugs.title: Python remote state stores transient token deltas
confirmed_bugs.expected: state.events should exclude transient StreamingDeltaEvent frames and match stored server history.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The client adds streamed deltas to state.events although the server persists none.

confirmed_bugs.title: Reading Python remote state twice corrupts its cached values
confirmed_bugs.expected: Repeated reads of confirmation policy, analyzer, agent and confirmation-mode flag should remain stable.
confirmed_bugs.actual: First reads are correct; second policy/agent reads raise ValidationError, analyzer becomes None and confirmation mode changes true to false.

confirmed_bugs.title: Python run join times out during a healthy long tool call
confirmed_bugs.expected: A second run() should join the 45-second tool call and return finished.
confirmed_bugs.actual: It raises ConversationRunError wrapping ReadTimeout after 30 seconds while the original run continues, writes its file and finishes.

confirmed_bugs.title: Python reconnect reconciles history but skips missed callbacks
confirmed_bugs.expected: A user message recorded during the socket outage should reach callbacks after reconnection.
confirmed_bugs.actual: Both messages appear in server history and state.events; only the connected message reaches the callback.

confirmed_bugs.title: Unimportable custom tool produces an unhandled server error
confirmed_bugs.expected: A client tool the server cannot import should result in a 4xx or a recorded conversation error.
confirmed_bugs.actual: Creation succeeds with 201, then sending the message fails with 500 for the unregistered tool.

confirmed_bugs.title: TypeScript RemoteWorkspace corrupts binary downloads
confirmed_bugs.expected: The five-byte file ff 00 80 fe 41 should download byte for byte with file_size 5.
confirmed_bugs.actual: FileClient returns the exact bytes; RemoteWorkspace produces eleven bytes ef bf bd 00 ef bf bd ef bf bd 41 and file_size 11.

confirmed_bugs.title: TypeScript GitChange status type disagrees with server values
confirmed_bugs.expected: Statuses returned by gitChanges should type-check against exported GitChange.status.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The server values UPDATED and ADDED type-check against generated GitChangeStatus but fail against the exported lowercase union.

confirmed_bugs.title: TypeScript BashWebSocketClient cannot open a Node socket
confirmed_bugs.expected: The Node callback should receive the BashOutput that the CLI replays on the same socket.
confirmed_bugs.actual: No frames arrive and onError says WebSocket implementation not available because the ESM module attempts require('ws').
notes: Two driving bullets share the ESM WebSocket constructor discovery failure and are counted as one defect.

confirmed_bugs.title: TypeScript updateConversation return type promises missing fields
confirmed_bugs.expected: The declared ConversationInfo result should include the conversation id and stored new title.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The title is stored, but the promise resolves with success:true and its id/title are undefined.

confirmed_bugs.title: TypeScript manager ignores conversation execution options
confirmed_bugs.expected: maxIterations 7 and stuckDetection false should be preserved, like direct RemoteConversation.start.
confirmed_bugs.actual: The manager-created conversation has max_iterations 500 and stuck_detection true.
